title: NY State Senate · District 30
area: Central and northern Manhattan: Harlem, East Harlem, Morningside Heights, Hamilton Heights, Washington Heights, and parts of the Upper West Side.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled; incumbent Cordell Cleare advanced on both lines without appearing on a primary ballot. The Republican primary was also canceled and, as of this writing, no Republican or other opposition candidate has filed for the general election, leaving Cleare unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Cordell Cleare
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed; no Republican or third-party opponent has filed for the general election.
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 30 (since November 2021)

priorities.text: Reparations and economic, environmental, restorative and racial justice.
"Truly affordable housing" and housing safety in her district.
Quality schools and equitable education, including accountability for charter schools.
Access to healthy foods for district residents.
Ending gun violence and domestic violence, and supporting workforce development and job creation.

record.text: Sponsored S10548, the Citizens Utility Board Act, which would create a board funded by voluntary consumer dues to represent residential utility ratepayers before the Public Service Commission, with a $1 million state appropriation for startup; in Senate Finance Committee as of May 20, 2026.

Sponsored S10578, extending brownfield redevelopment tax credits for a stalled project at 1800 Park Avenue in East Harlem; in Senate Investigations and Government Operations Committee as of May 26, 2026.

Sponsored S10341, establishing the Harlem Unified Community Planning urban renewal agency to enable community-driven local economic development planning; referred to the Senate Local Government Committee as of May 14, 2026.

Chairs the Senate Aging Committee in the 2025–2026 session and also sits on the Cities 1, Education, Corporations Authorities and Commissions, Housing, Investigations and Government Operations, and Social Services committees.
